Definition: accusative case singular of G4771; thee:--thee, thou, X thy house.
BiblicalUsage: Se is thee, the thee of direct address — the accented form of the word, set apart from the unaccented enclitic. Peter says it on the water — Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee — and Gabriel says it to Zacharias: I am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings. And Jesus prays it: that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the thee matters because it is personal: Peter speaks to the Lord, the angel speaks to the man, and the Son speaks to the Father — each by name, face to face.
